title: Getting started
summary: From a local repository to your first agent run.
text: Before you start  You need Git, a local repository, and Claude Code or Codex installed and signed in. Werkbord uses the agents and credentials already on your machine.  Joining a team? Start with  Team setup , then return here to prepare your own runner.  1. Install Werkbord  On a Mac, download   Werkbord-preview.dmg   and drag Werkbord to Applications. Or, from a terminal on macOS or Linux:   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/micho8cho93/werkbord/main/scripts/install.sh | sh   Either way Werkbord sets itself up, starts a background service, and shows you the board. Add a repository when prompted. See  installation  for requirements and Windows support.  2. Start a task  Open your project, choose  New task , and describe a small change. Choose your agent, then start the run. Werkbord keeps the task’s changes in an isolated Git worktree.  Try something easy to review, such as adding a test or fixing a small UI issue.  3. Review the result  Watch progress from the board. If the agent needs an answer or approval, open the task and respond. When it finishes, inspect the diff and test the change before merging.  Moving a card tracks workflow. Starting a run is a separate action. See  tasks and review  for the full flow.  Take it further    Connect your phone  Check runs and respond on the move.    Set up a team  Coordinate work across local runners.

title: Installation
summary: Install, update, and manage your local runner.
text:
The Mac app  The simplest way on a Mac: download   Werkbord-preview.dmg  , open it, and drag  Werkbord  onto  Applications . It is one app for Apple Silicon and Intel, for macOS 13 or later. This test preview is ad-hoc signed, not signed with a Developer ID or notarized by Apple. If macOS blocks it after the first launch attempt, open  System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway . From a terminal:   curl -fL -o ~/Downloads/Werkbord-preview.dmg https://github.com/micho8cho93/werkbord/releases/download/werkbord-v1.3.1-preview.1/Werkbord-preview.dmg
open ~/Downloads/Werkbord-preview.dmg   The first time you open the app it sets Werkbord up on your computer: the  werkbord  program in  ~/.local/bin , your data and database, and a background service that keeps your agents and schedules running after you close the window. Closing the window or quitting the app never stops them. It is the same Werkbord the command-line installer makes: install one and use the other and you have one installation.  Keep the app in  Applications . The preview has no automatic app updater. To replace it, download the signed Mac release when it is available and drag it to Applications. The signed release supports  Werkbord → Check for Updates…  and checks the update signature before installation. Updates wait while coding agents are working. Looking for updates can be turned off with  "noUpdateCheck": true  in  config.json .  Requirements  The Mac app needs only macOS 13 or later. The command-line installer below needs macOS or Linux, Git, and a signed-in Claude Code or Codex CLI. Run it from a terminal where your agent command works.  Command line: macOS and Linux   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/micho8cho93/werkbord/main/scripts/install.sh | sh   The installer verifies the release checksum, puts  werkbord  in  ~/.local/bin  (with  devboard , its earlier name, beside it), and sets up the local database, access token, and user background service. Browser setup handles repositories and optional GitHub integration.  If your shell cannot find  werkbord , add  ~/.local/bin  to your PATH and open a new terminal.  Windows  Native Windows support is experimental. In PowerShell:   irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/micho8cho93/werkbord/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex   Native Windows does not run the coding agents. To run agents on Windows, use the Linux installer inside WSL with Git and your agent installed there.  Check your setup   werkbord status
werkbord doctor
werkbord open   If the browser opens but agents are missing, run  werkbord setup  from the terminal where Claude Code or Codex works. The background service needs that environment too.  Update or remove  In the Mac app:  Werkbord → Check for Updates… . From a terminal:   werkbord update --check
werkbord update   Updates create an automatic database backup. Check  werkbord status  and  werkbord doctor  after updating.   werkbord uninstall  removes the installed service and binary while preserving your data. Use  the command reference  for service controls.

title: Agents and settings
summary: Choose how a task runs, without repeating your setup.
text: Connect your agents  Werkbord discovers installed Claude Code and Codex CLIs. Sign in through the agent’s own CLI first. Authentication stays with that agent on your machine.  If discovery fails, check the command in your terminal and follow  the agent troubleshooting steps .  Set useful defaults  Execution settings inherit in this order: global, project, task, then a one-run override. The most specific value wins. Set your usual agent at the global level and override it only where needed.   Agent default  lets the installed agent choose its model or reasoning setting. Available options come from the agents on your machine.  Choose an interaction style   Ask when needed  Let the agent pause for your input.  Autonomous  Reduce routine interruptions. Required approvals still need a person.  Stop if blocked  Stop when the task cannot continue without intervention.   Settings belong to a run  Each run records its selected settings when it starts. Changing a project default affects future runs. Use a one-run override to try a different agent or model without changing the task’s defaults.

title: Tasks and review
summary: Plan the change, run an agent, then decide what ships.
text: Write a useful task  Give the task a clear outcome, the relevant files, and a way to check the result. Choose the project and agent before starting. A small, verifiable change is a useful first run.  Follow the run  The board shows workflow; the run shows execution. A task can be in progress while its agent is running, waiting, or blocked. Moving a card does not implicitly launch an agent.  Open a waiting task to answer a question or approve a command. A blocked task needs attention before it can proceed.  Review before merging  Agent changes live in an isolated Git worktree. Open the diff, check the files touched, and run the project’s checks. Finishing a run does not merge it.  If it needs another pass, continue the task with more instructions. A continuation can reuse its worktree so the next agent has the existing changes.  Continue with another agent  Use  Continue with  to hand off a task for review or fixes. Keep the requested outcome explicit so the next run can pick up the work.  For shared ownership, claims, and reviewer sign-off, see  Team workflow .

title: Scheduling
summary: Plan work around time, dependencies, and available capacity.
text: Schedule a task  The calendar and board show the same tasks. Set a time in the scheduling form, including from your phone. Explicitly arm auto-run when you want the task to start automatically.  The controller handles scheduled work even with the browser closed. The computer and service must remain running.  Set dependencies  A task can wait for other tasks in the same project. Cycles are rejected. Completing a dependency makes the next task eligible; it does not transfer the dependency’s code.  Merge or otherwise integrate prerequisite changes in Git before expecting a dependent task to use them.  Control concurrency  Capacity defaults to  1  and can be set from  1 to 16 . Starting, running, waiting, and blocked runs consume capacity. Unknown or overlapping paths are serialized to avoid unsafe parallel work.  If the queue stalls, check waiting or blocked runs before raising the limit.  Missed or interrupted runs  Choose whether a missed schedule runs late or skips after its grace period. An interrupted attempt does not automatically rerun. Inspect the task and rearm it when you are ready.

title: Phone access
summary: Use the same board from your phone while work runs on your computer.
text: Connect both devices   Sign in to Tailscale during Werkbord setup.  Install Tailscale on your phone and sign in to the same account.  On your computer, display the connection QR code:    werkbord open --qr   Scan it with your phone. Keep your computer awake and online while agents are running. You can also open the connection with  werkbord open --phone .  Add it to your home screen  Open the HTTPS address, then use your browser’s  Add to Home Screen  option. HTTPS and MagicDNS must be enabled for your tailnet so installation and browser notifications can work.  An HTTP address can still travel over an encrypted Tailscale connection, but it does not enable the browser’s HTTPS-only features.  Keep the connection private  The phone link includes an access token. Treat it like a password and keep QR screenshots private. Tailscale controls network access; Werkbord still requires a token for remote access.  You can turn phone access off in Settings.  If the board will not open  Check that both devices are online, Tailscale is connected to the same account, and Werkbord is running. Run  werkbord doctor  on the computer for connection diagnostics.  For setup and certificate issues, see  troubleshooting .

title: Additional runners
summary: Send tasks to another machine you control.
text: Pair a runner  Use the same Werkbord version on both machines. Install and sign in to the agent CLI on the new machine, with the Git credentials it needs.  In  Settings → Runners → Add runner , choose its allowed projects. Run the generated  werkbord join  command on the new machine. Pairing codes expire after five minutes.  Bind a repository  Each runner needs its own local clone. Bind the project to its absolute path:   werkbord runner repo <project-id> /absolute/path/to/repository   Replace the placeholders with the project ID and real clone path. A project binding does not copy your repository or agent credentials.  Enable routing deliberately  A new runner starts with capacity 1 and automatic routing off. Verify the repository and agent before enabling it for work. Stop an unneeded controller on that machine if it is intended only as a runner.  Runners and Team  An additional runner executes your own tasks on another machine. Werkbord Team coordinates people and their local runners. For a shared team workspace, use  Team setup .

title: Team setup
summary: Create a workspace, invite people, and connect local runners.
text:
Before you install  These steps are for people with access to Werkbord Team. Each teammate runs agents on their own machine. The Team server coordinates tickets, reviews, and repository status.  Looking for access?  Join the Team waitlist .  1. Install the Team server   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/micho8cho93/werkbord/main/scripts/install-team.sh | sh   The installer places the  werkbord-team  executable on your machine. It does not create a background service or start a server.  2. Create a workspace   werkbord-team workspace create --name "Acme" --owner "Ada"
werkbord-team serve   Replace the example names with yours. Workspace creation prints an owner token and sign-in link once. Store them securely. The server runs in the foreground at  http://127.0.0.1:7430 .  3. Make it reachable  For other machines, serve on an appropriate network interface with  --addr  and put the server behind an HTTPS reverse proxy or on a trusted private network. Keep public access behind HTTPS; plain HTTP can expose tokens.  See  access and security  before sharing the server address.  4. Add a project  Open  Projects , create a project, and add its repository address. Each teammate will need a local clone with that Git remote.  5. Invite your teammates  Open the project’s  People & invites , create an invite, select a role and expiry, and share the code with its intended recipient. Codes are shown once and can be revoked. Each member gets their own access token.  A lost token can be reissued; the old token stops working.  6. Run your first ticket  Install  individual Werkbord  on each teammate’s machine. Add a local repository with the matching Git remote. Create a ticket in Backlog and promote it to Available. Claim it, then choose  Open in my runner .  Importing a handoff creates the local task. The agent starts when you start the run. Continue with  Team workflow .

title: Team workflow
summary: Keep ownership and review clear while everyone works locally.
text: From backlog to done  Backlog → Available → In progress → Review → Done  Prepare a ticket in Backlog, then make it Available when someone can pick it up. Claiming assigns one owner through a guarded operation, so two people cannot claim the same ticket at once.  Work in your local runner  Use  Open in my runner  on your claimed ticket. The handoff matches your local repository by Git remote. Review the imported task and start the agent yourself.  Your runner handles execution and files. The Team server does not run agents or receive your agent credentials.  Request a review  Move finished work into Review and ask a project reviewer to check it. A reviewer cannot sign off their own work unless they are the project owner. An open pull request prevents the ticket from reaching Done.  Resolve feedback in your local runner, then return the ticket for review.  Check repository status  The Repository view shows last-reported branches, conflicts, overlapping work, and branches behind the target. Use it to spot coordination problems early.  Status is a report, not a merge operation. Resolve conflicts and integrate changes in Git, then refresh the report.

title: Access and security
summary: Know what is shared and who can act on it.
text: What Team stores  Team stores coordination data such as tickets, reviews, membership, and repository status. Code execution and file contents stay with local runners. Agent and Git credentials stay on each person’s machine.  Project roles   Member  Pick up tickets and contribute work.  Reviewer  Review work and provide sign-off within the project.  Owner  Manage the project and its access.   Project membership scopes what a person can see and do. Review rules prevent ordinary reviewers from approving their own tickets.  Tokens and invites  Access tokens use 256 bits of randomness. Store them securely and give each person their own token. Reissue a lost token to invalidate it.  Invite codes are shown once, stored as hashes, and can expire or be revoked. An invite code is separate from the member’s personal access token.  Hosting and backups  The server binds to localhost by default. Use HTTPS when exposing it beyond a trusted private connection. Configure the data directory with  WERKBORD_TEAM_DATA_DIR .  The workspace lives in  team.db . For a running server, use SQLite’s  .backup  command to create a consistent snapshot rather than copying an actively written database file.  Board sync  Connected boards receive updates through long polling. Reconnecting clients reread the current state. In the product’s tests, board changes appear in under one second; network conditions affect real-world timing.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Start with the local service, then check the failing connection.
text:
Start here   werkbord status
werkbord doctor
werkbord logs -n 100   Status checks the service. Doctor checks setup and dependencies. Logs show recent activity. Keep tokens and private task details out of anything you share.  My agent is missing  Run  claude --version  or  codex --version  in your terminal. If the command is missing, fix the agent installation first. Confirm that the agent is signed in.  If it works in the terminal but not Werkbord, run  werkbord setup  there to refresh the service environment, then  werkbord restart .  The local page will not open  Check  werkbord status . Start a stopped service with  werkbord start , then use  werkbord open  to get the current authenticated link.  If it still fails, inspect doctor output and recent logs before restarting repeatedly.  My phone cannot connect  Keep the computer awake. Confirm that phone access is enabled and both devices are connected to the same Tailscale account. Generate a fresh link with  werkbord open --qr .  If the page loads but home-screen installation or notifications fail, check HTTPS and MagicDNS for your tailnet.  A scheduled task is not starting  Check that auto-run is armed, dependencies are complete, and capacity is available. Waiting and blocked runs still occupy slots. Inspect the missed-run policy and any interrupted attempt before rearming it.  A Team handoff cannot find my project  Check that individual Werkbord is running and that the local project has the matching Git remote. Import the handoff into that project. Importing alone does not start an agent.  For server or workspace setup, return to  Team setup .

title: Command reference
summary: The everyday commands for individual Werkbord and Team.
text:
Local service      Command  Purpose       werkbord setup   Configure repositories, agents, and the service.     werkbord status   Check the installed service.     werkbord start   Start the service.     werkbord stop   Stop the service.     werkbord restart   Restart the service.     werkbord open   Open the board.     werkbord open --qr   Show a phone connection QR code.     werkbord doctor   Check setup and dependencies.     werkbord logs -n 100   Read recent service logs.     werkbord update --check   Check for an update.     werkbord update   Update with a database backup.     werkbord uninstall   Remove the service and binary; preserve data.      Add a project   werkbord project add ~/code/my-app   Use the path to an existing local repository.  Team server   werkbord-team version
werkbord-team workspace create --name "Acme" --owner "Ada"
werkbord-team serve   Use  --addr  to choose the listening address.  WERKBORD_TEAM_DATA_DIR  selects the data directory;  WERKBORD_TEAM_LOG_LEVEL  and  WERKBORD_TEAM_LOG_FORMAT  control logging.  See  Team setup  before serving a workspace to other machines.
